record.paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
record.original_question: Characterize all finite line-segment configurations E that are edge-Ramsey: those for which, for every number of colors r, every sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space has the property that any r-coloring of its line segments contains a monochromatic copy of E.

evidence.quote: given some fixed finite configuration E of line segments

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A line segment in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is an unordered pair of distinct points $\{x,y\} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. Two finite sets of line segments in Euclidean spaces are called congruent copies of each other if one can be mapped to the other by a Euclidean isometry (preserving the segment structure).

Let $E$ be a finite configuration of line segments in some Euclidean space. Say that $E$ is edge-Ramsey if for every positive integer $r$ there exists an integer $N=N(E,r)$ such that, for every $n \ge N$, every coloring of the set of all line segments of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $r$ colors contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $E$ (i.e., a congruent copy of $E$ all of whose segments receive the same color).

Problem: Give a complete characterization of the finite line-segment configurations $E$ that are edge-Ramsey.
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys and recent expository works on Euclidean Ramsey theory list the characterization of edge-Ramsey configurations as a long-standing open problem. Only partial results are known: regular n-gons are edge-Ramsey for n=2,3,4, while the general classification remains unresolved, and no widely accepted conjectural characterization has been proposed.

status_evidence.title: The Biggest Open Problem in Euclidean Ramsey Theory (Patel, UChicago REU 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses edge-Ramsey sets and notes the characterization problem remains open with limited partial results.
status_evidence.claim: Characterizing edge-Ramsey configurations is an open problem; only special cases (e.g., small regular polygons) are known.

status_evidence.title: Euclidean Ramsey Theory (Handbook of Discrete and Computational Geometry, chap. 11)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys edge-Ramsey configurations and lists their characterization among the unresolved problems of the field.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization of edge-Ramsey configurations is unresolved in the standard survey literature.
